Read-only graph reduction analysis
Current root c6ebe7e lineage, src/graph.cpp grid_graph106-257; supplied block source and examples/catalog.json; recorded runtime artifacts/night-bulk-combined-acceptance/public20-azfhztyv/runtime.json. Requirements read fully. No compile, graph/numerical execution, reachability test, runtime modification or new timing performed. Python only read existing20case JSON and arithmetic formulas; no benchmark workload.

Decision: do not implement local redundant-edge pruning for this benchmark. A generic local WAW rule is sound, but removes zero edges from the scored blocked workload. The current scored grid graphs are already transitively reduced after per-destination sort/unique and extraction of Copy/ZeroUpper, by the source-access argument below. Additional global reachability is both unnecessary and unjustified. Never put the block-specific formulas below into runtime; they are offline reasoning tied to this input source only.

Generic local rule and caution:
Consider one exact partition cell with last writer W and all subsequent readers R1..Rk before next write T. Current builder adds W→Ri when each read is encountered. If at least one prior independent reader exists and T waits for every such reader, each W→Ri→T is a path, so a separate W→T contribution from this cell is redundant. Example: task0 writes X; task1 reads X and writes Y; task2 writes X. Existing edges0→1,0→2,1→2 may safely become0→1,1→2. This uses existing writer+reader state and needs no reachability structure.
For read-modify-write T, current processing adds T to readers after it already appended W→T on the read phase. A naïve 'readers nonempty' check sees T itself; T→T is filtered, so suppressing W solely because the reader list is nonempty is wrong. It must distinguish an independent reader from current ID, and removing W from the shared deps vector may remove an edge required by another cell. Correct deletion is per-access contribution before union, with all current read/write aliases handled. This is more than blindly changing one line.
Keeping only the most recent reader is also wrong: two reads R1,R2 after W need not depend on each other. A future write must wait for both. Their source order is not a happens-before relation. Cross-cell edges may sometimes order them, but that requires extra evidence not in the cell state; no generic shortcut from ID ordering alone.

Why that rule saves no blocked-case edges:
Each tile(i,j) is repeatedly read-modify-written by its update tasks. Between those updates no separate task reads that tile: the only reader is the same update which next writes it. Its final factor/trsm writes turn the tile into a panel input; afterwards many tasks read it, but that panel tile is never written again. Therefore every nonempty reader chain of independent tasks belongs to a tile that has no later write. At each numerical write, the reader chain contains only its own current task (or no prior task). The generic W→R→T pattern never occurs in the actual block source.

Why the remaining distinct prerequisites cannot be transitively removed (source-analysis notation only):
Let P_i be the diagonal factor task, S_{j,i} the panel solve for j>i, and U_{k,j,i} the update of trailing target(k,j), k>=j>i, during elimination step i.
- P_0 has no numerical predecessor; P_i (i>0) waits solely for the last update U_{i,i,i-1}. Its one edge is indispensable.
- S_{j,i} waits for P_i and, when i>0, the last update U_{j,i,i-1} of its own output. The latter tile is not read by any other task before S_{j,i} overwrites it, so it cannot have a path to P_i; P_i cannot reach the earlier update. Both prerequisites are independent and necessary.
- U_{k,j,i} waits for S_{k,i}, S_{j,i} (one unique source when k==j), plus the preceding update U_{k,j,i-1} if i>0. Same-step S tasks are independent siblings under P_i. The previous target update belongs to future column j>i: before current U it is not read by a panel task, and its next overwrite is current U. Its later factor/solve is at step j, so it cannot reach either step-i panel source. Conversely same-step panel sources cannot reach an earlier source-order update. Thus these immediate predecessors are pairwise incomparable.
In any DAG, edge p→T is redundant only if p reaches another immediate predecessor of T. Here no such pair exists for any task. This proves distinct edges in this particular block graph cannot be removed while preserving required reachability. Runtime remains generic and continues supporting arbitrary exact-grid access sequences.

Existing recorded counts, matching source-derived E(q)=q(q²-1)/2 for every parallel case:
q  numerical tasks  existing edges  after sound transitive reduction
4  20               30              30

The complete existing20case run constructs111276 edges (serial-small cases build none). q48 accounts55272, about49.7%. Recorded q48 tasks19602 include extracted Copy/ZeroUpper, not graph tasks. These exact agreements support the described dependency pattern, though the irredundancy argument is from source/access semantics rather than timing logs alone.

Duplicate candidate entries are different from graph edges:
Read-modify-write currently appends a last-writer candidate at read and again at write; repeated aliases can append it more than once. sort/unique already removes those, so they do not cause extra runtime decrements. A source-agnostic same-cell current-reader optimization could avoid some duplicate append/sort work, but would not change final edge count, Metadata, kernels or concurrency. This is not a reason to claim runtime edge reduction. It would need its own measured builder-only evidence and is outside the requested no-implementation decision.

Benefit ceiling:
For the proposed WAW or transitive-edge removal on this scored source, removable edges=0; reduction in CSR bytes/decrements/edge callbacks=0. Thus mechanism benefit upper bound is exactly0, regardless of q. Do not spend a new A/B slot on it.
For any unrelated future builder optimization, root's diagnostic all-batch graph cost~7ms and q48~3.7ms are loose absolute ceilings only if all graph work could disappear. Edge pruning cannot remove region validation, grid discovery, state traversal or task interpretation, and here it cannot remove edge work either. Large-b execution is already dominated by unchanged kernels per diagnosis; no unsupported broad speedup expectation.

Scope/requirements: no hardcoded graph, no case special casing, no new metadata/security audits, no additional permanent tests. Keep P010; prioritize the separately justified alignment/address hypothesis. This report finishes this direction without a source change.
